plan.planning_summary: This plan initiates the first of two allowed research rounds for a two-layer antireflection coating. Since no literature evidence is available (evidence_ids_allowed is empty), the routes are theory-based, relying on fundamental thin-film interference principles. The core hypothesis is that a specific ordering of SiO2 and TiO2 layers, optimized within the 40-160 nm thickness bounds, can minimize the mean reflectance over the 450-700 nm band. Two complementary routes are proposed: Route 01 tests the 'High-Low' sequence (TiO2 then SiO2) on glass, which acts as a stepped index transformer. Route 02 tests the 'Low-High' sequence (SiO2 then TiO2) on glass. Both routes treat layer thicknesses as continuous design variables to be optimized by a deterministic solver under the specified constraints. The execution requests explicitly define the stack topology, material indices, wavelength range, and optimization bounds.

routes.title: Optimization of TiO2/SiO2/Glass High-Low Antireflection Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack with the higher-index material (TiO2, n=2.40) adjacent to the glass substrate (n=1.52) and the lower-index material (SiO2, n=1.46) facing air will provide a smoother effective index transition than the reverse order, potentially yielding a lower mean reflectance across the visible spectrum when thicknesses are optimized.
routes.design_principle: Stepped refractive index matching: Air (1.0) -> Low (1.46) -> High (2.40) -> Substrate (1.52). This attempts to bridge the large index gap between air and the intermediate/high layers before reaching the substrate.
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thicknesses strictly bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm
Exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave transformer approximation as an initial guess heuristic
expected_advantages: The high-index layer next to the glass may reduce the reflection coefficient at the second interface compared to a direct SiO2-Glass interface.
Two degrees of freedom (thicknesses) allow tuning for broadband performance.
known_risks: The index step from SiO2 (1.46) to TiO2 (2.40) is large and may cause significant internal reflection if not perfectly tuned.
Thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the theoretical global minimum if it lies outside this box.
Two layers may be insufficient to achieve the <0.03 target over such a wide bandwidth.
routes.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar three-medium stack: Incident Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 (SiO2, n=1.46, lossless), Layer 2 (TiO2, n=2.40, lossless), Substrate Glass (n=1.52, lossless). Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2 to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm (5 nm spacing). Constraints: Thickness of Layer 1 in [40, 160] nm; Thickness of Layer 2 in [40, 160] nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Maximum 64 solver evaluations. Report the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.

routes.title: Optimization of SiO2/TiO2/Glass Low-High Antireflection Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack with the lower-index material (SiO2, n=1.46) adjacent to the glass substrate (n=1.52) and the higher-index material (TiO2, n=2.40) facing air may offer superior broadband performance by creating a different interference condition that better averages out reflections across the 450-700 nm band.
routes.design_principle: Alternative index profiling: Air (1.0) -> High (2.40) -> Low (1.46) -> Substrate (1.52). This places the largest index jump at the air interface, potentially utilizing the high-index layer as a strong phase shifter.
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thicknesses strictly bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm
Exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Destructive interference conditions for dual-layer systems
expected_advantages: Placing the high-index layer first might allow for thinner overall optical thickness while maintaining phase shifts required for cancellation.
May yield a different spectral shape (e.g., double-hump vs single-hump) that results in a lower arithmetic mean.
known_risks: The large index mismatch at the Air-TiO2 interface (1.0 to 2.40) creates a high baseline reflection that the second layer must cancel, which is difficult over a broad band.
Same thickness bound risks as Route 01.

Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2 to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm (5 nm spacing). Constraints: Thickness of Layer 1 in [40, 160] nm; Thickness of Layer 2 in [40, 160] nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Maximum 64 solver evaluations. Report the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.

research_influence: No external literature evidence was provided (evidence_ids_allowed is empty). Consequently, the routes are derived entirely from first-principles theory regarding thin-film interference and index matching strategies.

The strict constraint of exactly two layers and specific materials (SiO2, TiO2) dictated the creation of two mutually exclusive topologies (Route 01 and Route 02) to ensure both possible permutations are tested within the limited round budget.
unresolved_decisions: Whether the 40-160 nm thickness window is sufficient to achieve the <0.03 mean reflectance target for either topology.
Which of the two layer orders provides the global minimum for this specific material pair and bandwidth.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
